Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns:

Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 8 \\ -4 & -6\end{aligned}].$ You're given that ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2$ are the eigenvalues of $A$, and
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$, ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are the respective eigenvectors. Find the matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=A,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=2,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Diagonalizing a 2x2 Matrix Given Its Eigenvalues
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 8 \\ -4 & -6\end{aligned}].$ You're given that ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2$ are the eigenvalues of $A$, and
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$, ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are the respective eigenvectors. Find the matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=A,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=2,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.problem:
Consider the matrix $H$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
H=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ b & c\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & a\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ b & c\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$
after.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=4,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 7 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
H=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 7 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 7 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}.
$$

 

In conclusion, we get  $a=-2,$ $b=7,$ and $c=1.$

content.knowledge_point: Diagonalizing a 2x2 Matrix Given Its Eigenvalues
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $H$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
H=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ b & c\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & a\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ b & c\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$
content.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=4,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 7 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
H=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 7 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 7 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}.
$$

 

In conclusion, we get  $a=-2,$ $b=7,$ and $c=1.$
